title: Intel Pentium II
description: Famous for moving away from the traditional socket design to the massive 'Slot 1' SECC cartridge. It brought high-performance multimedia capabilities to consumer desktops.

title: Intel Pentium III
description: Introduced the controversial 'processor serial number' and the highly impactful SSE instruction set, drastically improving floating-point and multimedia performance.

title: Intel Pentium 4 (180nm)
description: The dawn of the NetBurst architecture. Intel sacrificed raw efficiency to chase massive clock speeds, famously pushing past the 1 GHz barrier with incredibly long data pipelines.

title: Intel Pentium 4 (130nm)
description: Codenamed 'Northwood', this refinement added more cache and introduced Hyper-Threading to desktop PCs, allowing the OS to treat one physical core as two logical brains.

title: Pentium Dual-Core E2200
description: Intel dropped the NetBurst heating problems and pivoted to the highly efficient 'Core' microarchitecture. This budget chip offered true dual-core performance to the masses.

title: Intel Core 2 Duo E7500
description: Built on the 45nm 'Wolfdale' core, this processor ran incredibly cool while offering massive L2 cache, making it a legendary overclocker and gaming CPU of its era.

title: Intel Core i3-2100
description: The 'Sandy Bridge' architecture was a massive leap. It fully integrated the graphics processor (GPU) and memory controller directly onto the same silicon die as the CPU.

title: Intel Core i3-3220
description: Codenamed 'Ivy Bridge', this introduced 3D Tri-Gate transistors at a microscopic 22nm scale, drastically reducing power leakage and packing over a billion transistors.

title: Intel Core i5-6500
description: The 'Skylake' architecture brought native DDR4 memory support to the mainstream. As a true quad-core, it handled heavy multitasking and demanding AAA games with ease.
